issues.legal_issue: A statutory discretion to restrict execution of eviction decrees does not violate equal protection when the enactment supplies sufficient guidance through its policy and purpose.
material_facts: The challenged enactment required prior permission before an eviction decree concerning a building in a slum area could be executed.
The enactment’s stated purposes and operative provisions addressed both improvement and clearance of slum areas and protection of tenants from eviction.
The challenge argued that the authority had no statutory criteria governing whether permission should be granted.
issues.conclusion: The discretion was sufficiently guided by the enactment’s policy and purpose, so the provision did not violate Article 14.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 14, a law that gives an authority discretion without any declared policy, intelligible purpose, or guiding standard may permit arbitrary discrimination. Guidance need not be set out expressly in the particular provision conferring discretion; it may be derived from the preamble, surrounding circumstances, other operative provisions, and the enactment’s object. The Court applied the principles discussed in Ramakrishna Dalmia v. Justice Tendolkar, Harishankar Bagla v. State of Madhya Pradesh, M/s. Dwarka Prasad Laxmi Narain v. State of Uttar Pradesh, State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar, Kathi Raning Rawat v. State of Saurashtra, Kedar Nath Bajoria v. State of West Bengal, and Pannalal Binjraj v. Union of India.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_eviction_con: A proceeding challenges a legal regime that conditions execution of eviction decrees on administrative permission.
predicates.law_targets_slum_clearance_and_tenant_pr: The law seeks both to improve or clear slum areas and to protect their residents from eviction.
predicates.administrative_discretion_is_guided_by_l: The authority’s discretion can be guided by the law’s stated policy, purpose, and related operative provisions.

issues.definition: When a challenge to eviction control concerns a law with both slum-improvement and tenant-protection aims, and the law guides the authority’s discretion, the discretion does not violate equal protection.

issues.legal_issue: Leaving the application of a law to an administering authority is not an excessive delegation of legislative power when the legislature has stated the law’s policy and purpose.
material_facts: The enactment left the competent authority to decide, after an inquiry, whether permission to execute an eviction decree should be granted.
The enactment’s preamble and operative provisions identified the purposes of slum improvement and clearance and tenant protection.
The challenge argued that the legislature had delegated power without prescribing detailed criteria for each eviction case.
issues.conclusion: The delegation was not excessive because the legislature had indicated the policy and purpose that guided the authority, and it was not required to prescribe every detail of the law’s application.
issues.legal_principle: The essential legislative function is to determine legislative policy and enact it as a binding rule. When the legislature states the policy and purpose of a law, it may leave its detailed application and the determination of relevant facts to designated authorities; the law need not specify every possible case. The Court relied on the delegation principles discussed in Harishankar Bagla v. State of Madhya Pradesh and the authorities considered in its Article 14 analysis, including Ramakrishna Dalmia v. Justice Tendolkar.

predicates.challenge_to_delegated_administrative_po: A proceeding contends that the legislature improperly delegated its lawmaking power to an administrator.
predicates.legislature_has_stated_policy_and_purpos: The legislature has identified the objectives and policy that the law is intended to advance.
predicates.authority_applies_policy_to_individual_c: The authority applies the law’s policy when deciding how it applies to particular cases.

issues.definition: When a delegation challenge concerns a law whose policy and purpose are stated and whose authority applies that policy to individual cases, the delegation is not excessive.

issues.legal_issue: A restriction on a landlord’s ability to obtain possession of property is reasonable when it serves the public interest in protecting slum residents, is guided by legislative policy, and operates with procedural safeguards.
material_facts: The enactment restricted execution of eviction decrees for buildings in slum areas unless the competent authority first granted permission.
The restriction sought to prevent residents without alternative accommodation from being displaced while slum improvement and clearance were pursued.
The authority’s decision was subject to an appeal, and the statutory process included an opportunity for the tenant to be heard and an inquiry.
The challenge argued that the restriction was unreasonable because it could operate for an indefinite period and interfere with the landlord’s ability to possess and use the property.
issues.conclusion: The restriction was reasonable and in the interests of the general public; its indefinite duration did not make it invalid given its temporary character in purpose, the circumstances addressed, and the procedural and appellate safeguards.
issues.legal_principle: Article 19(1)(f) protected the right to hold property, but Article 19(5) permitted reasonable restrictions in the interests of the general public. Reasonableness must be assessed in the context of the social problem the legislature addressed, including the restriction’s relationship to its purpose, its practical operation, and the safeguards governing its application. The Court held that protection of slum residents and orderly elimination of slums justified the restriction, and that the appeal and inquiry procedures helped ensure compliance with the law’s policy.

predicates.challenge_to_property_right_restriction: A proceeding challenges a restriction on an owner’s ability to obtain possession of property.
predicates.eviction_is_limited_to_protect_residents: The restriction is intended to prevent residents lacking other accommodation from being displaced.
predicates.restriction_advances_public_welfare: The restriction is connected to improving or clearing unhealthy housing conditions and protecting residents.
predicates.administrative_decisions_have_procedural: The decision-making process provides an opportunity to be heard, an inquiry, and review by an appellate authority.

issues.definition: When a property restriction protects residents without alternative housing, advances public welfare, and is administered with procedural review, the restriction is reasonable.

issues.legal_issue: A special law governing eviction from buildings in slum areas applies in addition to the general rent-control law.
material_facts: The landlord had obtained eviction decrees under the rent-control law for buildings situated in an area declared to be a slum area.
The special law required prior permission to execute an eviction decree concerning a building in a slum area, notwithstanding other law.
The rent-control law also contained an overriding clause, while the special law contained its own overriding provision.
issues.conclusion: The special law applies to buildings in declared slum areas in addition to the rent-control law, including where an eviction decree has been obtained under the rent-control law.
issues.legal_principle: The Court read the special law’s provision requiring prior permission to execute an eviction decree together with its overriding clause and the rent-control law’s overriding clause. It concluded that the special law operates additionally for buildings in declared slum areas, and that its application is engaged when a decree for eviction is to be executed.

predicates.proceeding_concerns_execution_of_evictio: The proceeding concerns whether an eviction decree may be carried out.
predicates.building_is_in_declared_slum_area: The building is situated in an area formally designated for special slum-related treatment.
predicates.general_rent_law_governs_the_decree: The eviction decree was obtained under the law that generally regulates landlord-tenant eviction.
predicates.special_housing_law_requires_permission_: A special housing law requires permission before the decree can be executed notwithstanding other law.

issues.definition: When execution of a rent-law eviction decree concerns a building in a designated slum area and a special housing law requires permission despite other law, the special law applies alongside the general rent law.
